status: THROWAWAY EXPLORATORY RUN — owner-requested, not a merge candidate
preregistration: This file plus criteria.json ARE the pre-registration of record. Both are committed BEFORE any generation cell is run; the commit ordering plus the per-cell UTC timestamps in outputs/ make precedence checkable off the records themselves.
question: Does loading the third-party skill `writing-plans` change the QUALITY OF FEEDBACK a model gives on a real strategic planning document, does the size of that change differ by model, and how consistent is each model's output from run to run? Direction unstated. A null is an equally valid recorded outcome.
owner_framing: Owner, 29-Jul-2026: 'I want to see the difference writing-plans makes in terms of effect size for each model type, and how consistent the output is with and without writing-plans... The output I'm interested in is the quality of feedback on the plan document for each run.'

task.input: plan.md — a verbatim frozen copy of the owner's active plan ~/.claude/plans/2026-07-28-repo-state-consistency-alignment.md as it stood 29-Jul-2026 10:47
task.instruction: The following is a planning document. [...] Give the author your feedback on this plan.
task.framing_rule: The prompt names NO desirable property of feedback. Naming any would leak the rubric into the prompt, inflate every arm equally, and destroy the instrument's ability to discriminate.

lanes.copilot: copilot -p --model auto — `--model <id>` is entitlement-gated on this account and rejects every explicit id including every haiku spelling (measured 29-Jul, see README). Owner direction: run auto and record the answering model per cell. The `auto` router resolved to gpt-5-mini on the probe call.

haiku_note: The owner asked for 'haiku 5'. No such model exists; Haiku 4.5 (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001) is the latest Haiku. That lane runs 4.5.

arms.wp: the writing-plans body (obra/superpowers @ d884ae04edeb, v6.1.1 MIT, 7,092 bytes, YAML frontmatter stripped) PREPENDED to an otherwise byte-identical task prompt

arm_symmetry: The prompt for each arm is constructed once and its sha256 prefix recorded on every cell, so byte-identity across lanes and reps is checkable from the records. Identical tool denial (all tools stripped), identical neutral cwd, identical timeout, identical pinned CLAUDE_EFFORT=medium on the Claude lanes. Arms differ ONLY in the prepended skill body.
injection_choice: UNIFORM PROMPT-PREPEND on every lane, NOT each CLI's native system-prompt flag. Claude offers --append-system-prompt and grok offers --rules, but copilot has no equivalent. A per-lane injection mechanism would confound the cross-model effect-size comparison, which is the owner's primary question. Labeled limitation: this measures the skill body as prepended context, which may differ from system-prompt loading.
no_tools_rule: Every lane runs with tools stripped and from an empty scratch cwd outside the repo. Rationale: the owner requires context identical run-to-run, and tool carve-outs are NOT equivalent across the three CLIs, so live exploration would confound the model comparison with a CLI-plumbing comparison. Labeled limitation: this measures feedback given fixed context, not tool-directed exploration.
env_hygiene: The harness runs under Claude Code with CLAUDE_EFFORT=xhigh and CLAUDE_CODE_* variables set. clean_env() strips them and pins effort to medium; inherited unchanged they would have given the three Claude lanes a reasoning budget the grok and copilot lanes never get.
dependent_variable: fraction of the pre-registered binary criteria in criteria.json marked met by a blind judge. Criteria are authored from the PLAN AUTHOR's needs; the treatment skill's own checklist (TDD, bite-sized steps, DRY/YAGNI, frequent commits, checkbox syntax, exact paths, no-placeholders) was read only to ensure no criterion mirrors it, because a criterion restating the treatment would measure leakage rather than quality.
secondary_metrics: response_chars per cell (verbosity is the leading rival explanation for any effect)
per-criterion met-rate by arm and lane (mechanism attribution)

blinding.rule: Judges receive the feedback text and the plan document only — never the arm, the lane, or the model. Blind ids are sha256-derived (skill-bench lib/blind.py).
blinding.tell_stripping: The writing-plans body MANDATES an arm tell: 'Announce at start: I'm using the writing-plans skill'. It also emits `superpowers:` sub-skill references, `docs/superpowers/plans/` paths, and a two-option execution-handoff offer. All are stripped before grading, and the strip rate is recorded per arm. Without this the judge would identify the treatment arm directly and the whole measurement would be worthless.

judging: Two judges grade every cell independently: grok-4.5 and claude (opus). NEITHER is fully independent of this generator set — three lanes are Anthropic models and one lane is grok — so per-judge results are reported SEPARATELY with same-family pairings flagged, and no verdict is promoted on a single judge. A verdict that flips between judges is labeled exploratory.

analysis.per_cell: mean and standard deviation of fraction-met over the 3 reps — the consistency figure the owner asked for.
analysis.per_model: delta = mean(wp) - mean(bare), two-sample t interval on df=4, reported WITH its own mde80 so a null is read as 'this design could only reliably call an effect of X or larger', never as 'no effect exists'.
analysis.pooled: two-way (model x arm) with model as a blocking factor: arm main effect and model x arm interaction on pooled within-cell error df=20. This is far better powered than five separate n=3 t-tests and directly answers 'does the effect differ by model'.
analysis.reporting_rule: Every comparison reports its mde80 alongside its point estimate and interval. The claim 'not significant at n=3, therefore the effect is negligible' is affirming the null and is NOT a conclusion this design supports; what it supports is 'this comparison could only reliably detect an effect of mde80 or larger'.

power_note: At 3 vs 3 the smallest reliably detectable effect is 3.03 standard deviations (two-sided 95%, 80% power, df=4). Whether that is useful depends entirely on the measured within-cell SD, which is why SD is a reported deliverable and not a nuisance parameter. The July 2026 writing-plans run recorded within-cell spread of exactly 0.0, which if repeated here would make n=3 adequate for a July-sized effect (+0.167); a within-cell SD of 0.15 would instead make it able to bound nothing.

cost.estimate_note: 30 generation cells: fable5 ~$0.30, opus5 ~$0.20, haiku45 ~$0.04 per cell (6 cells each); grok and copilot are subscription-billed and report no per-call dollar figure. Judging: 60 calls, grok notional, claude ~$0.10/call. Projected real total $7-10. Pilot first per ADR 0066; halt for re-approval if the pilot projects above 2x.

amendment_2026_07_29_tool_denial.when: After the 5-cell bare pilot, BEFORE any grid cell. The pilot is what surfaced it — the grok pilot cell narrated 'I'll read the plan against the repo', which a fully tool-denied cell cannot do.
amendment_2026_07_29_tool_denial.finding: Tool-denial flags are NOT portable across these three CLIs, and two of the three lanes were running unsandboxed. MEASURED with a planted-file probe: (a) grok's `--disallowed-tools` is a NO-OP — a probe cell read the planted file and returned its contents, both with grok's real lowercase tool names AND with the CamelCase names skill-bench/scripts/lib/judge.py passes; (b) copilot's bare `--available-tools` flag likewise did not strip tools, and `--available-tools=none` merely pushed the model onto `curl file://`; (c) claude's `--disallowedTools` with deny_tools.txt DOES hold — the probe answered 'CANNOT READ'.
amendment_2026_07_29_tool_denial.fix: grok switched to the ALLOW-list form `--tools todo_write` (probe: 'CANNOT READ'); copilot switched to `--excluded-tools=` with the full tool vocabulary read back from the CLI itself (probe: planted value never returned, zero tool-invocation events). Both verified by re-probe before the grid.
amendment_2026_07_29_tool_denial.blast_radius: The 5 pilot cells ran under the ineffective flags. Their working directory was an empty scratch dir outside the repo, so nothing was reachable by relative path and no cell returned repo content absent from plan.md — but the grok and copilot pilot cells were DISCARDED and re-run under the corrected flags rather than reused.
amendment_2026_07_29_tool_denial.upstream: This is also a live defect in the SHIPPED skill-bench library: lib/judge.py's GrokJudge passes CamelCase names to `--disallowed-tools` and CopilotJudge passes the bare `--available-tools`, so neither judge backend is sandboxed as its docstring claims. Out of scope for this throwaway branch; reported to the owner.
amendment_2026_07_29_tool_denial.residual: Every cell now records tool activity (copilot: tool-invocation event count; claude: num_turns) so hermeticity is evidenced per cell rather than assumed from a flag.

criteria_audit: criteria.json draft-1 (18 criteria) was adversarially audited before any spend by four independent lenses — treatment bias, judgeability, ceiling/floor discrimination, and confounds/gaming — and replaced by the hardened 20-criterion final-1 set. The audit found 6 draft criteria saturating in both arms, 4 mirroring the treatment's own habits (rigged-for), and 1 rigged-against. Its predicted bare-arm mean for the final set is 0.55.
gate_not_powered: PRE-REGISTERED FRAMING: this is an EXPLORATORY GATE, not a powered KEEP/CUT study. The cluster unit for the cross-model question is MODELS, G=5, below the G>=8 threshold the plan under review itself establishes. No result here promotes a skill decision on its own.

kill_conditions.ceiling: If the realised bare-arm mean is >= 0.80, the instrument is INSENSITIVE at this task and the run is reported as such — a null under a ceiling is NOT evidence of no effect.
kill_conditions.floor: If the realised bare-arm mean is <= 0.20, the criteria are too hard to discriminate and the same applies in the other direction.
kill_conditions.correctness: No arm may be promoted to a positive verdict if its mean false-assertion count exceeds the other arm's, regardless of fraction met. A confabulated review that scores well on form is a worse review, and C3 alone caps that penalty at 0.05 which is below noise.
kill_conditions.judge_flip: A main-effect verdict that differs between the two judges is labeled EXPLORATORY and no verdict is promoted.
kill_conditions.blinding: Any residual arm tell surviving tells.py halts grading outright (grade.py exits). A judge that can identify the arm invalidates the measurement.
kill_conditions.copilot_routing: The copilot lane's `auto` router resolves per call. The resolved model is logged per cell. If it varies WITHIN the copilot lane, that lane's delta is reported as descriptive only and excluded from the interaction test, because its arms would then differ by model as well as by treatment.

length_confound_rule: The treatment appends ~7.1k characters of doctrine that pushes toward more structure and broader section coverage, so response length is the leading rival explanation for any positive effect. response_chars is a PRE-REGISTERED covariate reported alongside every effect. If the correlation between score and length across the 30 cells exceeds 0.5, the arm delta is additionally reported restricted to length-matched cells and labeled descriptive. There is no length-matched placebo arm; that is recorded as an uncontrolled confound.
subset_reporting: Headline mean-fraction-met is reported alongside three pre-registered subsets (criteria.json:subsets): content_bearing, structure, and task_fit. An effect present in the full set but ABSENT in the content-bearing subset is verbosity or formatting transfer, not feedback quality, and is reported as such.
blinding_scope_decision: tells.py strips IDENTITY tells only (the mandated announcement, the skill name, `superpowers:` namespaces, the prescribed save path, REQUIRED SUB-SKILL directives). It deliberately does NOT strip STRUCTURAL markers the treatment encourages (checkbox syntax, Consumes/Produces blocks, Global Constraints headers): stripping those would alter the artifact being judged and delete real content. They are MEASURED instead (treatment_marker_hits) so structural transfer can be separated from quality analytically. Consequence, stated rather than hidden: a judge may still infer the arm from structure. blindcheck.py measures how often it actually can.
known_underpowered_by_design: At 3 reps the per-model comparison borrows a pooled error term across all ten cells (df=20), which lowers the per-model detectable effect from 3.03 to 2.40 pooled SDs. It is still a large-effect-only comparison. This is accepted deliberately: the owner asked for 3 runs, reps are the right lever for the VARIABILITY deliverable, and every comparison reports its own mde80 so no null is over-read.
limitations: ONE task. The effect estimate is specific to feedback on THIS document; it does not generalise to feedback on planning documents in general. Generalising would need several distinct documents as clusters.

writing-plans is a plan-AUTHORING skill being measured on a plan-REVIEW task. The plausible mechanism is that it supplies a normative model of what a good plan contains, which a reviewer can then review against. A null is therefore a reasonable prior, not a surprise.

The document under review is a strategic portfolio plan, not a code implementation plan, so the treatment's code-plan conventions may transfer badly. Criterion 6 exists to catch that and can move against the treatment.
No judge is outside all five generator families.
